title: Six markets, on paper
summary: Where the same three situations break, market by market: six sectors with their two traits, each opening in place to the one line that says where it breaks there — type and hairlines on paper, with the photos, network graphs and AI-image slot gone.

reference.site: Approved Kelwin system: homepage fit/U (the ledger on paper, the head column at the left)
reference.borrowed: The kit ledger that opens in place, one row at a time, with the section's head held in a left column so the rows hang from the heading's first line.
reference.kelwin: Same family as the homepage 'Who it's for' it is reached from, but its own job: markets, not criteria. Chips carry each market's two traits; an open row shows its line and nothing else. No drawing, no red, no second statement.

motion: entrance: label, heading and lede rise; the six rows cascade 80ms apart; then I·01 opens (≈1.25s, 360ms) — its open height is kept from the first frame, so nothing below moves. This is one of the page's two body play-once moments (the other is none: the situations and the close are still beats).
interaction: rows are buttons (aria-expanded / aria-controls), one open at a time, clicking the open row closes it; closed panels are inert.
on the live site: plays once as it scrolls into view. Reduced motion: I·01 open at once, no timers.
story: Deepens the situations the reader has just recognised with the sector detail the homepage doesn't carry: the same three situations, sharpest in committee-decided markets, so a buyer can find his own market and its typical break before he reaches who is sent away.
